goal: Add deterministic deliverable verification to trail_runtime.py's check gate, so a Checker's PASS claim can't stand if listed deliverable files don't actually exist on disk.
steps: 1. cmd_check: after validating verdict is PASS/FAIL, if the incoming frame has a 'deliverables' list (repo-root-relative paths), resolve each against the actual repo root and check existence; collect any missing

2. If any deliverable is missing, force the recorded verdict to FAIL regardless of what the caller claimed, and record a 'deliverables_verification' block in the written 04-check.json documenting what was checked and what was missing - never silently accept a false PASS, never silently drop the caller's original claim either (both are recorded)

3. If all deliverables exist (or none were listed - the field is optional, backward compatible), record deliverables_verification with checked=true and no missing entries, verdict passes through as given
4. Update the create-skill/scaffold-skill/pmcro-checker SKILL.md guidance to mention the new optional deliverables field where relevant (small doc update, not required for the mechanism itself)

5. Self-test: run trail_runtime.py open/plan/make/check end-to-end with a deliverables list pointing at (a) real files - confirm verdict passes through, (b) a nonexistent file - confirm verdict is forced to FAIL even when the frame claims PASS
success_criteria: A check frame with verdict:PASS and a real, existing deliverable path is recorded as PASS
A check frame with verdict:PASS and a nonexistent deliverable path is recorded as FAIL, with the missing path documented
No deliverables field: fully backward compatible, existing behavior unchanged
This is a genuine CLI change to a load-bearing governance script - self-tested directly, not assumed
out_of_scope: Enforcing this repo-wide retroactively on old sealed trails - immutable, never touched
grounded_in: .pmcro/runtime/trail_runtime.py (read in full), .pmcro/laws/laws.yaml's L-EVIDENCE and 'Checker Gates are Deterministic' invariant, live feedback from Shawn this session
